en.name: Hot peppers
en.summary: Hot peppers covers fresh chillies as a group, from bird's eye to cayenne. Kept dry and whole they last about a week in the fridge from the day of purchase, and frozen they keep good quality for about 9 months — though they lose their crispness on thawing.
en.pantry: Fresh chillies will sit out for a few days without becoming unsafe, but they shrivel steadily as they lose water through their thin walls. There is no room-temperature figure given here and none should be assumed. What room temperature is genuinely good for is drying: threaded on a string in a dry airy place, small thin-walled chillies dry rather than rot, which is a preservation method in its own right.
en.fridge: Fresh whole peppers will last longer if kept dry — that is the single most useful thing to know about them. Store them unwashed in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in a paper bag or a box lined with kitchen paper rather than sealed in plastic where they sweat, and about a week from purchase is the figure. Keep them whole: a cut or bruised chilli rots from the wound outward, and the wound is also where mould takes hold.
en.freezer: Chillies freeze easily and need no blanching. Wash, dry, and pack them whole into a sealed bag with as little air as possible at −18 °C (0 °F), where they keep good quality for about 9 months. Peppers lose their crispness when frozen and thawed, so this is a method for cooking chillies rather than for garnishes. Frozen chillies are also much easier to chop finely than fresh ones.
en.thawing: Do not thaw chillies — chop or slice them straight from the freezer. Thawed pods go soft and weep, and they will not hold a clean slice. Wash your hands or wear gloves regardless: freezing does nothing to the heat.
spoilage: Soft, wet or collapsing patches, usually starting at the stem
White, grey or black mould at the stem end or in a crease
Slimy skin rather than dry and taut
A fermented or sour smell instead of a fresh vegetal one
tips: Keep them dry above all else; moisture is what ends a bag of chillies.
Store whole and unwashed, and rinse only when you cook.
Freeze whole in a bag — no blanching, no stemming, no seeding.
String thin-walled chillies up to dry if you have more than you can use.

faq.q: How long do fresh hot peppers last in the fridge?
faq.a: About a week from the day of purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, kept dry and whole. Moisture is what shortens that.
Yes, whole and unblanched at −18 °C (0 °F) for about 9 months of good quality. They thaw limp, so use them in cooking rather than raw.
The fridge gives about a week and keeps them usable. Drying them is the other good option, especially for small thin-walled chillies.

faq.q: Do chillies get hotter as they age?
faq.a: Not really — but as they dry and shrink, the same amount of capsaicin sits in less flesh, so a wrinkled chilli can taste sharper by weight.

zh.name: 辣椒
zh.summary: 辣椒泛指各種新鮮辣椒，從朝天椒到長條的卡宴椒都算。保持乾燥、整根不切，冷藏從購買當天算起約可放一週；冷凍則可維持約 9 個月的良好品質，只是解凍後會失去脆度。
zh.pantry: 新鮮辣椒放在室溫幾天不會有安全問題，但果壁薄、會持續失水而皺縮。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。室溫真正擅長的其實是「乾燥」：把小型薄壁辣椒串起來掛在乾燥通風處，它會慢慢乾掉而不是爛掉，這本身就是一種保存法。
zh.fridge: 保持乾燥的整根辣椒放得比較久，這是關於辣椒最有用的一句話。請不清洗，裝在紙袋或鋪了廚房紙巾的盒子裡放進 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，不要密封在塑膠袋裡悶出水；從購買日起約一週。請保持整根完整：切過或碰傷的辣椒會從傷口往外爛，而傷口也正是黴菌著床的地方。
zh.freezer: 辣椒非常好冷凍，而且不需要汆燙。洗淨擦乾，整根裝進密封袋、盡量把空氣擠掉，放 −18°C，品質可維持約 9 個月。辣椒冷凍解凍後會失去脆度，所以這是給烹調用的做法，不適合拿來當盤飾。另外，冷凍的辣椒其實比新鮮的好切得多。
zh.thawing: 辣椒不要解凍——直接從冷凍狀態切片或切碎。解凍後會軟爛出水，也切不出漂亮的形狀。不論如何請戴手套或事後洗手：冷凍完全不會降低辣度。
spoilage: 出現軟塌、滲水或塌陷的部位，通常從蒂頭開始
蒂頭或皺摺處長出白色、灰色或黑色黴
表皮變得黏滑，而不是乾爽緊實
有發酵味或酸味，而不是新鮮的青椒味
tips: 最重要的就是保持乾燥；濕氣是一整袋辣椒的終結者。
整根不清洗保存，要煮之前再沖。
整根裝袋冷凍即可——不用汆燙、不用去蒂、不用去籽。
用不完的薄壁辣椒可以串起來風乾。

faq.q: 新鮮辣椒放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、保持乾燥且整根完整，從購買當天算起約一週。縮短它的主要原因就是濕氣。
可以，整根不汆燙放 −18°C，品質可維持約 9 個月。解凍後會軟，請用於烹調而非生食。
冷藏大約給你一週，狀態也比較好。另一個好選擇是風乾，尤其是小型薄壁的品種。
其實不會。但隨著它乾燥縮水，同樣的辣椒素集中在更少的果肉裡，所以按重量算，皺掉的辣椒吃起來可能更嗆。
